note: Who can answer each control (G-83). NIST's model, in this product's words: a COMMON control is provided centrally and inherited by everything that uses the provider — nobody's project decides whether multi-factor authentication is enforced. A SYSTEM-SPECIFIC control is about this activity and only the people doing it can answer. A HYBRID control is both: the platform provides part and the activity provides the rest. This decides who is asked, and it is the reason a requester was answering ten questions about the enterprise estate that they had no way to answer. The reasons are the owner's to ratify; they encode assumptions about which teams run what.

controls.because: an enterprise identity service defines and enforces entitlements; a project consumes them
multi-factor authentication is switched on for the estate or it is not
privileged access is separated and monitored centrally, not per activity
recertification campaigns run against the directory, across everything in it
joiners, movers and leavers are handled once for the organisation
remote entry is governed by the same identity and network estate for everyone
segmentation and boundary protection belong to the network estate
an edge or application firewall protects everything published through it
denial-of-service absorption sits at the edge, ahead of any one service
the platform secures the transport and the gateway; the activity secures its own interface design and authorisation
disk and transport encryption come from the platform; field-level encryption and key custody choices belong to the activity
a secrets manager is central; what an activity puts in it, and rotates, is its own
media handling and destruction is a facilities and endpoint matter for the whole estate
what data an activity collects and how far it can be reduced is a design choice only it can make
how long this activity's data must be kept, and why, depends on what it is for
log collection and retention are provided by the central logging service
continuous monitoring and alerting run across the estate, not per project
scanning and remediation service levels are set and run centrally
malicious code protection is deployed to the estate
patch cadence is an estate-wide programme
the testing programme and its cadence are central; scoping this activity into it is the activity's own
backup infrastructure is central; the recovery objective for this activity is its own decision
the incident response capability is central; this activity's escalation path and severity criteria are its own
continuity arrangements are provided; which tier this activity needs is its own
screening standards are set once and applied on hire
security awareness training is an organisation-wide programme
supplier physical access to our sites is governed by facilities for all suppliers
the assurance programme is central; obtaining and reading this supplier's evidence is the activity's own
the contract and its flow-down terms are specific to this engagement
which subcontractors this supplier uses, and whether that is acceptable here, is specific
what this supplier may reach in this activity is decided here
how this model was validated, and against what, cannot be answered centrally
who oversees this system's output, and how they intervene, is designed here
bias testing is against this use and this population
the documentation is of this system and its decisions
output quality is judged against what this activity is for
what personal information reaches prompts and outputs depends on this design
what this agent may act on is a boundary drawn for this activity
the platform enforces retrieval against the signed-in person permissions; whether this index is permissioned correctly in the first place is the activity own
the provenance of this model's training data is particular to it
how an affected person challenges this system's output is designed here
the lawful basis is for this processing, not for the organisation in general
serving a data-subject request depends on what this activity holds and where
the notice describes this processing
special-category handling and profiling safeguards are particular to this use
what this activity communicates, and to whom, is reviewed for this activity
which borders this activity's data crosses is a fact about this activity
the statutory and reporting obligations follow from what this activity does
the approval and any risk acceptance are for this activity
who oversees this activity, and reports on it, is set here
the procedures describe how this activity is run
